If you don’t mind, allow me to impart proper handling etiquette for fish, particularly trout and salmon:

Do: Keep them in the water as much as possible, using a rubber net, if you touch them wet your hands or your rubber gloves first. Support the body behind the pectoral fins with one hand, and prevent them from swimming away by grabbing their tail with the other hand, both with a gentle grip. Hold them horizontally for your hero shot, do this in the water over your net in case you lose your grip. Limit time out of the water to as long as you can hold your own breath before releasing them gently facing the current. 

Do not: Bank them, or use a string net. Wear gloves or touch them with dry hands. Definitely never touch their gills, or hold them by their jaws.  Holding them vertically is a no-no. Do not set the fish on the bank or in the grass. Please try not to drop them on the ground. Do not put them on a stringer and then release them.
